developments: Bitcoin held its rebound through Saturday evening, trading between about $59,660 and $60,450 on Kraken since the afternoon edition and near $60,260 at 21:30 UK, up about 0.5%.
ZEC was steady too, near $790 at 21:30 UK against about $785 at the afternoon edition, inside a range of about $778 to $798.
CoinDesk reported that Glassnode said Friday's sell-off cleared the largest cluster of futures liquidation levels, between $59,000 and $62,000.
briefing.changed: Little has moved since the afternoon edition. The rebound above the old $57,700 summer low has held for a second session, with no new market-moving news, so the picture is the same: a weekend recovery that US markets have not yet tested.
briefing.question: Does the rebound hold when US stock futures reopen on Sunday evening and US stocks and ETFs trade again on Monday?
briefing.watch: US stock futures reopen at about 23:00 UK on Sunday, then the US open at 14:30 UK on Monday. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Bitcoin holds above $60,000 in a quiet Saturday evening
lead.standfirst: Bitcoin kept most of Saturday's rebound into the evening, trading in a narrow band around $60,000 as traders waited for Monday's reopening of US markets.
body: Bitcoin traded near $60,260 on Kraken at 21:30 UK time on Saturday, Kraken data showed, about 0.5% above the level at the afternoon edition. Since 16:30 UK it has stayed between about $59,660 and $60,450.

CoinDesk reported that Bitcoin had risen more than 9% from an early low of $55,130, its weakest since September 2024. It cited Glassnode as saying Friday's sell-off had cleared the largest cluster of futures liquidation levels, between $59,000 and $62,000.

CoinDesk also reported about $1.1 billion of net withdrawals from US spot bitcoin ETFs over the past week. QCP Capital told it that a lasting recovery needed stable technology shares, calmer rates and a return of institutional money.
Zcash was steady near $790 on Kraken, inside a range of about $778 to $798 since the afternoon.
US stock futures reopen on Sunday evening, and US stocks and ETFs on Monday, the first test of the weekend's moves.

headline: A quiet evening: Bitcoin held near $60,260 and ZEC near $790, keeping Saturday's rebound. The test is the reopening of US markets on Sunday night and Monday.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, evening edition, Saturday the twenty first of November. A quiet evening. Bitcoin has held its rebound and is near sixty thousand two hundred and sixty dollars, up about half a percent since the afternoon, in a narrow range. Zcash is steady near seven hundred and ninety dollars. Analysts at Glassnode say Friday's sell-off cleared the biggest cluster of leveraged positions. The test comes when US stock futures reopen around eleven on Sunday night, and when US markets open at half past two on Monday afternoon. The next big event is the Fed decision on the ninth of December at seven in the evening. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $60,260 through a narrow evening range
stories.why: Kraken showed Bitcoin between about $59,660 and $60,450 since 16:30 UK and near $60,260 at 21:30 UK. CoinDesk put the bounce at more than 9% from a low of $55,130. The new evidence is that the reclaimed $57,700 summer low has held for a second session, though on thin weekend trading.

note.read: A tight range after a sharp rebound suggests forced selling has paused and the market is waiting for US investors rather than finding new buyers.
note.alt: Calm weekend trading says little; Monday's ETF flows and tech shares could restart the selling.
note.change: A drop back below about $57,700 when US markets reopen would undo the overshoot reading.

stories.title: Glassnode: sell-off cleared the biggest liquidation cluster
stories.why: CoinDesk reported Glassnode as saying Friday's fall cleared the largest cluster of futures liquidation levels, between $59,000 and $62,000, and CryptoQuant's Darkfost calling it extreme capitulation. CoinDesk counted about $1.8 billion of liquidations in 24 hours, $1.3 billion of them long bets. Less leverage near the price means fewer forced trades to amplify the next move.
stories.caveat: CoinDesk's $1.8 billion liquidation total is lower than the $2.67 billion Bitcoin.com News reported this afternoon; both cite CoinGlass, over different 24-hour windows.

note.read: With the big leverage cluster gone, the next move depends more on spot and ETF demand than on liquidations.
note.alt: New leverage can build quickly on a rebound, recreating the same risk within days.
note.change: Rising open interest with flat price through Sunday would suggest leverage is rebuilding.

stories.title: ZEC steady near $790
stories.why: Kraken showed ZEC between about $778 and $798 since the afternoon edition and near $790 at 21:30 UK, up from about $785. No new ZEC news since the afternoon.

stories.title: ETF outflows still the open question for Monday
stories.why: CoinDesk put last week's net withdrawals from US spot bitcoin ETFs at about $1.1 billion, with Friday's IBIT figure still pending; Bitcoin.com News earlier gave more than $1.25 billion for Tuesday to Friday. Nothing new until US markets trade on Monday.
stories.caveat: The two outlets' weekly totals differ and cover different days.

stories.title: Cyber bridge hit by suspected $1 million exploit; Upbit and Bithumb pause CYBER transfers
stories.why: The Block reported that 5.2 million CYBER tokens were minted on Solana at about 16:13 UK and moved out of the Ethereum bridge, with most sold for about $968,000 in ETH. Upbit and Bithumb suspended CYBER deposits and withdrawals, and CYBER fell about 8%. A second bridge incident in a day after Chainflip, a reminder of cross-chain risk.

investigating: Is leverage rebuilding on the rebound? Evidence: Bitcoin futures open interest and funding rates on Sunday compared with Saturday.
How large were Friday's US spot bitcoin ETF outflows? Evidence: Friday's IBIT figure and SoSoValue or Farside daily totals.
Will Monday's US session confirm the bounce? Evidence: Sunday night's Nasdaq futures, then Monday's Nvidia move and ETF flows.
